feature_id.description: On the sheet: the feature that granted this action, matching features[].feature_id. Absent for item actions. Ignored in content.

resource_id.description: On the sheet: the granting feature's limited-use resource, matching resources[].feature_id. Usually the same as feature_id; a resource attached to a feature's spells is keyed feature:<id>. Absent when there is none. Ignored in content.

Character.description: A character's stored state: choices made and things that change in play. Everything derived (AC, bonuses, attacks) is on the Sheet.

acknowledgements.description: Warnings the user has marked as intentional, matched by key.

background_id.description: A feature tagged background. List them at /api/content/backgrounds and set this with PATCH.

classes.description: One entry per class, in the order taken. The first is the character's starting class.

coins.description: Currency id to amount. Negative means owed.

details.description: Descriptive free text: alignment, appearance, personality and so on. The rules engine never reads it. A PATCH can change one field, e.g. {"details":{"faith":"Mielikki"}}.

modifiers.description: Ad hoc modifiers on this character, applied on top of those from features and items.

portrait_url.description: A link to an image for the character, http or https. The server stores the link only; the browser loads the image. Clear it with null in a PATCH.

race_id.description: A feature tagged race. List them at /api/content/races and set this with PATCH.

selections.description: Choices made on features. Change them with the selections endpoints.

spellbooks.description: Spell choices per source id, for example class:wizard.

error.description: Set when the stored data couldn't be read.

portrait_url.description: The character's portrait link, if set.

eligible.description: False when the character doesn't qualify. Frontends decide whether to hide or grey out the option.

feature_id.description: The instance id, as used by resources, selections and actions. A repeatable feat taken twice has two ids.

granted_by.description: The feature whose grant or choice added this one, for example the ASI feature a feat was picked from. Absent for top-level features.

level.description: The class level it was gained at. Absent for features that don't come from a class.

resource_id.description: Its limited-use resource, matching resources[].feature_id. Absent when it has none.

source.description: The feature's own origin, or else the class, race or background it was reached through. other when neither says.

source_id.description: The class, race or background it belongs to. A feat with no source of its own gives its own id.

container.description: The id of the entry this one is stored in.

custom.description: A one-off item defined inline, used instead of item_id when set.

proficient.description: Weapons: proficient with this one weapon regardless of weapon_profs, for example a Pact of the Blade weapon. Pair it with ability_override cha.

container.description: The id of the entry this one is stored in. Empty at the top level.

container_info.description: Present when the entry is a container, even an empty one. capacity is the weight it holds (0 or absent = no limit); ignores_contents_weight means its contents add nothing to carried weight (Bag of Holding).

contents.description: Containers only: total weight of everything stored inside, including nested containers, whether or not it counts toward carried weight. Absent means 0. Compare with container_info.capacity.

dice.description: Makes this a dice rider (for example 1d6 Sneak Attack), shown on attacks rather than added into numbers.

Sheet.description: Everything the rules engine computes for a character. Never stored; recomputed on every request.

ac_detail.description: Which AC formula was used, and every alternative with whether it was eligible.

actions.description: Actions granted by features and equipped items. Those from a feature carry its feature_id and, if it has limited uses, a resource_id matching resources[].feature_id.

attacks.description: Computed attacks for equipped weapons, feature-granted attacks, and an unarmed strike.

carry.description: Carried weight against capacity, and the encumbrance state.

caster_level.description: Combined caster level for multiclass slot tables. Pact casters don't count.

features.description: Every feature the character has, from classes, subclasses, race, background, feats and choices, in the order they resolved. The race and background themselves are listed too.

inventory.description: Resolved inventory entries with names, weights, costs and containers.

notes.description: Situational modifiers, advantage and disadvantage, and reminders that don't change a number.

pact_slots.description: Pact magic slots. Absent when the character has none.

pending_choices.description: Choices the character is entitled to but hasn't made. Drives level-up flows. Fill them in with the selections endpoint.

resources.description: Limited-use feature resources with uses spent.

spell_slots.description: Shared spell slots. Pact slots are separate.

spellcasting.description: One entry per spell source: classes, plus features and items that grant spells.

wallet.description: Coins by denomination and their total value in base units.

warnings.description: Rules problems found in the character. The API never rejects these: show them, and let the user acknowledge ones that are intentional.

acknowledged.description: True if the character has an acknowledgement matching this key.

key.description: A stable identifier. Use it to acknowledge the warning.

info.description:
A rules engine and storage service for D&D-style characters, built to be driven by any frontend.

## The core ideas

- **Character vs sheet.** You store a *character*: the choices made and the things that change in play. The server computes the *sheet* from it (AC, bonuses, attacks, spell DCs, carrying weight). You never calculate rules yourself; fetch the sheet.
- **Everything is permissive.** Rules problems (a skill outside the allowed list, spending a slot you don't have, a prerequisite not met) are never errors. The request succeeds and the sheet carries a `warnings` entry. Show warnings, and let the user acknowledge ones that are intentional (homebrew, DM rulings).
- **Pending choices drive wizards.** `sheet.pending_choices` lists every choice the character is entitled to but hasn't made (starting skills, a subclass, an ability score improvement, spells to pick). For each, ask `choice-options` for what's allowed, then record the pick with `selections`.
- **Feats and ability score improvements.** At a feat level the character makes one choice: a feat. Ability Score Improvement is one of the feats, and taking it opens a second pending choice for the two points. That second choice's `feature_id` looks like `ability_score_improvement@rogue_asi_4:feat`, which names the pick it belongs to, so a feat taken twice has two separate sets of points. Always use a `feature_id` exactly as `pending_choices` gives it.
- **Backgrounds and races.** Both are features marked with a tag (`background`, `race`), chosen by setting `background_id` or `race_id` on the character with a PATCH. List the choices at `/api/content/backgrounds` and `/api/content/races`. A background's own picks, such as its ability score increase and any feat it grants, appear in `pending_choices`. So does choosing a race or a background at all (`feature_id` `character`, `choice_id` `race` or `background`) when the loaded content offers any. Ability score increases come from the background; a race does not change ability scores.
- **Actions return the sheet.** Every play action responds with the updated sheet, so the screen can redraw without a second request.
- **Content comes from packs.** Class, item, spell and feature ids come from `/api/content`. Homebrew packs layer over the core one, so the id lists can differ between servers.
- **Strict bodies.** Unknown fields in a request body are a 400, so a typo can't silently drop data.

## Building a character

1. `POST /api/characters` with a name and ability scores.
2. `POST /api/characters/{id}/level-up` once per level.
3. `GET /api/characters/{id}/sheet` and read `pending_choices`.
4. For each pending choice, `GET .../choice-options` then `POST .../selections`.
5. Pick spells by patching `spellbooks` on the character, for example `{"spellbooks": {"class:wizard": {"cantrips": ["fire_bolt"]}}}`.
6. Add gear with `POST .../inventory` and money with `POST .../coins`.
7. `POST .../rest` with `long` to start at full health.

## Errors

Every error has the shape `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}` with codes `bad_request`, `invalid_id`, `not_found`, `already_exists`, `bad_conversion`, `method_not_allowed`, `not_supported` and `internal`.

## Notes

- There is no authentication; it is meant to run locally or on a trusted network.
- Browsers on another origin need the server started with `-cors-origin`.
- Actions on one character are serialised, so concurrent play actions don't overwrite each other. `PUT` and `PATCH` are last-write-wins.

post.description: Send exactly one of `gain`, `spend`, `pay` or `convert`. Spending is exact: the named coins leave, and a shortfall leaves a negative balance with a warning rather than failing. `pay` is a price paid by value from whatever coins are held, largest first, with change: `{"pay":{"gp":15}}` from 10 gp and 100 sp leaves 50 sp. If the coins held are worth less than the price, `pay` fails with 400 code `cant_afford` and nothing changes. `convert` makes change (for example 1 pp to 10 gp) and fails with 400 if the result isn't a whole number of the target coin. Currencies come from /api/ruleset.
